Indispensable upgrade to the classic slow cooker When my old slow cooker committed suicide (our neighbor's construction work caused the inner stoneware liner to leap off of the drying rack and shatter on the floor), I took advantage of the opportunity to upgrade to an Instant Pot. I'd been hearing so much about how fast and easy they make cooking. The first week I had it, I made a different recipe in it every night. Lasagna, macaroni and cheese, hearty mushroom and barley stew, and many others. We quickly realized that the Instant Pot cooks pasta completely differently from the regular method of boiling it. And it tastes amazing. The pasta cooks through completely, yet remains substantial to the bite. We cook all of our pasta in the Instant Pot now, even if it's just spaghetti, not a full meal. We've sautéed in it, steamed, pressure cooked, and even made rice. Everything came out perfectly. I think I'd prefer to sauté things on the stovetop, simply because I don't like reaching down into a hot pot to stir things. But if you're a college student with no stove, it gives you a great option for more styles of cooking. One helpful tip I'd add is when releasing the pressure valve, make sure your Instant Pot is well away from walls and windows. Otherwise, you'll have to clean starchy water stains off of them. Now, I make sure it's got plenty of clearance, and that there's nothing on the counter that I don't want getting wet, and it's fine. I just wipe up the moisture that condenses as part of kitchen cleanup. We love the instant pot so much, we haven't put it away since we got it! We use it a couple of times a week at least.

An effective low-cost expander I have a relatively new Mac Mini M4, and I do find its ports somewhat limiting. The Mac has two USB-C in front and three Thunderbolt ports in the back. Because the Mac mini itself is so small and light, it can be difficult to access the ports and plug peripherals in and out. This UGreen USB hub works connected either to the USB ports in the front or to one of the Thunderbolt ports in the back. It doesn’t offer Thunderbolt speed, but it is quite quick and responsive for USB-C. I have had minor reliability problems with the ports on the M4—I have a USB keyboard, trackball, backup drive, and sometimes two external SSD drives plugged in, and the Mac itself sometimes doesn’t see everything at the same time—for instance, my trackball sometime disappears. I’ve had this hub plugged into one of the USB-C ports in front and keep a number of peripherals plugged into it, and they have all worked very effectively at the same time, and the speed has been very responsive on the external data drives. So it has improved my Mac. This is not heavy; it’s light plastic, but it works well. What I would have appreciated is if this had one USB-A port, too. I see a lot of USB-A hubs that have one C and a lot of As, but the new standard is USB-C. Some of my peripherals are USB-A, and I have little adapters that convert USB-A to USB-C and those work great with this, too, so with one of those, you can, of course, plug USB-A items into this. This has been very helpful to me with my M4 Mini and I recommend it.

Makes a noticeable difference! When my elderly cat (18 this summer! Cat tax included in review) was diagnosed with asthma, it meant that all three of us who live in my apartment (my husband and I plus cat) all have some sort of allergy or respiratory issues from different things. I've always had allergies to things like dust and pollen, and my husband had recently developed a cough and post nasal drip that the doctor could find no particular cause of. I happened to be browsing on Prime Day after looking into air purifiers and got this one for a very affordable 60 bucks. The reviews said it worked great just out of the package and setup was easy, and they were right. No assembly, nothing to fuss with. Just remove the plastic from the filter, pop it back in and plug it in. The difference was noticeable very quickly. Husband has basically stopped coughing and his post nasal drip has reduced significantly. I also noticed he isn't snoring anywhere near as loudly as he was before. My own allergy symptoms have alleviated; my sinuses used to feel stuffy which made it harder to fall asleep, but that's basically solved. My own post nasal drip has also noticeably improved. Even my cat's asthma noises have improved. I'm sort of shocked to encounter a product that actually noticeably solves a problem. Shortly after buying it, I had a small fire in my oven. Everything was okay, but the smoke was obviously a problem. I decided to put the air purifier on the counter to see what the number went up to- 130! But about an hour later, the number on the panel read about 10 or 12, and the normal range for my apartment is between 5-17. It has a sleep setting, but we keep it on 1 during the night because it's so quiet. I like to keep it on 2 during the day because it's still just light background humming. One thing I thought was nice is that there's a QR code on the side of it to link you to the correct filters to buy when you need to replace them. However, out of all the things that could actually use an app, it doesn't have one. It could be nice to have a really simple one that records the PM number so you could have an idea of the air quality patterns in your home. At the same time, it's refreshing that it doesn't have one lol My apartment is 1,300 square feet so technically this little guy should be making some difference on the whole thing, but it might be better to have it in a more central location for that; I like it in the bedroom though, since it's made such a difference in our symptoms that were impacting our sleep, and my cat mostly stays in the bedroom so it just makes sense for us. 10/10, really happy with it!
